text:
alex: Heads-up — I sketched a proposal for per-org dashboards + a gating signal for noisy neighbors. Need infra + runtime inputs before I put this in the product board. TL;DR: per-org view, tenant isolation flags, noisy_neighbor_score, quota breach timeline, and routing fallback metrics.

maria: thanks alex — can you list the concrete metrics you need from runtime vs infra? I want to separate UX panels (what product shows) from the ingest contract.

alex: sure. Runtime needs to export per-request labels: org_id, model_variant, route_decision (primary/fallback), batch_size, kv_cache_hit(boolean), tokens_in, tokens_out, inference_latency_ms. Infra needs: host_id, gpu_id, queue_depth, concurrent_sessions, memory_pressure_pct, preemptions. Also a derived noisy_neighbor_score computed from queue spikes + p50 latency delta.

sam: FYI collecting per-request labels at full resolution will be heavy. Propose counters + histograms aggregated per minute with label cardinality capped to (org_id, model_variant, route_decision). For noisy neighbor detection we can emit a sampled high-res trace when queue_depth > 80% for > 10s.

jon: are we comfortable with per-org ids in telemetry (PII concern)? ops: we must ensure org_id is hashed or uses an internal tenant key. RBAC on dashboards too.

kevin: we can use tenant_id (hashed) in metrics and map to real org in the console via RBAC lookup. Metrics pipeline already supports a hashed_label option.

anna: UX ask — product wants a single "Org Insights" page: top row KPIs (requests/min, cost_estimate, p50/p95 latency), mid row heatmap (model usage by variant), bottom row: noisy neighbor timeline + action buttons (throttle, route override, support ticket). Need the exact fields for the buttons to call the internal APIs.

alex: buttons will call internal endpoints: POST /internal/tenants/{tenant}/actions with body {action, scope, reason}. Example: {"action":"route_override","scope":"org","params":{"preferred_model":"gptx-8q"}}. We should include a small audit event emitted to infra on every button press.

sam: API looks fine. For routing override we need to know live capacity and fallback rules before honoring. We should surface a boolean "can_override" on the dashboard which is computed by a short-circuit policy: capacity_ok && !ongoing_rollout.

maria: product needs the telemetry schema so frontend can render. Can sam paste sample PromQL/SQL snippets for the panels?

sam: pasted example PromQL for p95 latency per org (assuming org label is tenant_hash):

```
# p95 latency per tenant per 1m
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant_hash))
```

and a noisy neighbor score (simple):

```
# noisy_neighbor_score: normalized sum of queue spikes and latency delta
(sum(rate(queue_spike_count[5m])) by (tenant_hash) * 0.6) +
(sum(increase(latency_above_baseline_count[5m])) by (tenant_hash) * 0.4)
```

kevin: we should also track model_fallback_count per tenant. Frontend panel will show fallback count/s and last_fallback_time. Metric: `sum(rate(model_fallback_total[5m])) by (tenant_hash)`

jon: ops note: dashboards must not expose tenant_hash mapping to users who don't have permission. Console will only resolve to org name if viewer has RBAC role. Otherwise show anonymized id.

maria: good. UX: show anonymized id + ability to "request access" — that hits support flow. Also need ability to toggle between 1m/5m/1h rollups.

alex: question on noisy neighbor alerting: should we emit per-tenant alerts at infra level or keep it in platform? I lean infra-level alerts (pager if SLA impacted) and platform-level alerts for UX signals only.

sam: agree — infra alerts on host-level saturation, platform alerts when tenant's noisy_neighbor_score > threshold AND customer-tier==paid. We'll need a tag for customer-tier in metrics or the mapping service.

kevin: mapping service can add a `tier` label during enrichment. That won't increase cardinality in stored raw metrics (we'll only join at query time).

anna: small UX nit: when there is an active noisy neighbor we want a timeline + suggested actions: "request throttling", "schedule dedicated", "open support". Suggested actions should call the internal API with audit.

alex: agree. Also for tenant isolation gating we need an internal feature flag: `org_insights_ui` and `org_isolation_mode` to gate rollout. We should do a canary on 5% orgs first.

sam: we'll provide a telemetry endpoint and a small ingestion contract doc. Example ingestion contract (flattened):

```
# telemetry ingestion contract v1
metric labels: tenant_hash, model_variant, route_decision, instance_pool, host_id
aggregation: 1m rollups, 5m rollups for dashboards, 1h rollups for billing
sensitive: tenant_hash must be hashed on client side
sampling: high-frequency requests may be sampled at 1/10 for raw traces, but counters/histograms must be accurate
```

maria: can we get an ETA? product wants a mock in two weeks for the design review.

sam: infra can deliver the PromQL and a sample metrics bundle in 7 business days. We'll also add a small feature to emit `noisy_neighbor_signal` events to the event bus for sampling.

kevin: mapping + RBAC work is 5 business days. Audit events pipeline hooking is 4 days.

alex: ok — I'll create a GH PR with the dashboard wireframes + the front-end API spec. Will tag everyone. Can we decide on the alert thresholds now? Propose noisy_neighbor_score > 10 for info, > 25 for warn, > 50 for critical.

jon: those numbers are arbitrary until we have baseline data. Let's make the thresholds configurable per-cluster and start with lower sensitivity in canary.

maria: agreed. final asks before I schedule the design review: 1) sample metrics + PromQL (sam) 2) API spec for action buttons (alex) 3) RBAC mapping doc (kevin) 4) draft canary plan + gating (alex + sam). If we have those in 7 days, we can meetup.

ops-bot: deploybot: will monitor ingestion config changes. If you push contract changes to infra/telemetry the bot will run validation checks.

alex: thanks all — I'll spin up the PR and assign owners. :thumbsup:
